question: Should OpenClaw accept the Installed Apps legacy opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout once the branch is refreshed?
rationale: The code path is a plausible and focused fix, but disabling prior opt-ins and tying the release to Play Console/Data Safety materials is an upgrade and release-policy choice that automation should not make.

options.title: Accept reset and rollout
options.body: Approve the privacy-protective legacy opt-in reset, verify the external Play/privacy materials, resolve conflicts, and land the branch.

options.title: Revise disclosure first
options.body: Request wording, placement, or consent-state changes if Play review or product policy needs a different prominent disclosure shape.

options.title: Hold for release materials
options.body: Pause the PR until Play Console state, Data Safety CSV, privacy policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept reset and rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the privacy-protective legacy opt-in reset, verify the external Play/privacy materials, resolve conflicts, and land the branch.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android and Android release-lane history makes this the best available owner for the branch-refresh and rollout decision.
